Family Planning.question: 1) An eligible couple means a currently married couple where the wife is in the reproductive age group of:
Family Planning.exp: Eligible couple refers to a currently married couple where the wife is in reproductive age group. The file mentions 15–45/49 years. Use of contraception is not necessary to define eligible couple.

Family Planning.question: 2) A target couple is best defined as an eligible couple who has:
Family Planning.option1: 2–3 living children and not using contraception
Family Planning.option3: No living child and wants pregnancy
Family Planning.option4: 4 or more children and using contraception
Family Planning.exp: Target couple is a subset of eligible couples. They have 2–3 living children. They are currently not using contraception.

Family Planning.question: 3) Spacing methods are mainly used to:
Family Planning.exp: Spacing methods are temporary and reversible. They are used to postpone pregnancy or increase birth interval. They may be used by both sexes.

Family Planning.question: 4) Terminal methods are mainly intended for:
Family Planning.exp: Terminal methods are permanent contraceptive methods. They are suitable for couples who have completed family size. Decision must be informed and voluntary.

Family Planning.question: 5) Barrier methods mainly prevent pregnancy by:
Family Planning.exp: Barrier methods block sperm entry mechanically or chemically. They prevent sperm from reaching the ovum. Examples include condom, diaphragm and spermicides.

Family Planning.question: 6) Male condom is best classified as:
Family Planning.exp: Male condom is a physical or mechanical barrier. It blocks sperm entry into female genital tract. It also protects against STI including HIV.

Family Planning.question: 7) Which barrier method also protects against sexually transmitted infections including HIV?
Family Planning.exp: Male condom gives dual protection. It prevents pregnancy and reduces transmission of STI including HIV. This is an important advantage over many other contraceptives.

Family Planning.question: 8) Spermicidal creams and jellies are examples of:
Family Planning.exp: Spermicides are chemical barrier methods. They are used intravaginally. They immobilize or kill sperm.

Family Planning.question: 9) Condom with spermicide is an example of:
Family Planning.exp: Combined barrier method uses both physical obstruction and spermicidal action. Condom with spermicide is an example. Diaphragm with spermicide is another example.

Family Planning.question: 10) Diaphragm with spermicide combines:
Family Planning.option2: Tubal occlusion and cervical mucus thickening
Family Planning.exp: Diaphragm provides mechanical blockage. Spermicide immobilizes or kills sperm. Together they form a combined barrier method.

Family Planning.question: 11) IUCDs are placed inside the:
Family Planning.exp: IUCDs are intrauterine contraceptive devices. They are long-acting reversible methods. They are placed inside the uterine cavity.

Family Planning.question: 12) Lippes loop is an example of:
Family Planning.exp: Lippes loop is a first-generation IUCD. It is non-medicated or inert. It is historical and less commonly used now.

Family Planning.question: 13) Cu-T 380A is an example of:
Family Planning.exp: Cu-T 380A is a second-generation copper IUCD. Copper enhances contraceptive effect. It acts by spermicidal action and local endometrial reaction.

Family Planning.question: 14) LNG-IUS belongs to:
Family Planning.exp: LNG-IUS is a third-generation IUCD. It releases levonorgestrel. It thickens cervical mucus and suppresses endometrium.

Family Planning.question: 15) Progestasert is a:
Family Planning.exp: Progestasert is a hormone-releasing IUCD. It releases progesterone locally. It acts mainly by cervical mucus and endometrial changes.

Family Planning.question: 16) The main contraceptive action of copper IUCD is due to:
Family Planning.option1: Spermicidal action and local endometrial reaction
Family Planning.exp: Copper increases contraceptive efficacy. It has spermicidal action. It also produces a local endometrial reaction.

Family Planning.question: 17) Hormone-releasing IUCD mainly causes:
Family Planning.option1: Thick cervical mucus and endometrial suppression
Family Planning.exp: Hormone-releasing IUCD releases progesterone or levonorgestrel. It thickens cervical mucus. It also suppresses the endometrium.

Family Planning.question: 18) Suspected pregnancy is a contraindication to:
Family Planning.exp: IUCD should not be inserted in suspected pregnancy. Other contraindications include active pelvic infection and unexplained genital bleeding. Proper screening before insertion is important.

Family Planning.question: 19) Active pelvic infection is a contraindication to:
Family Planning.exp: IUCD insertion is contraindicated in active pelvic infection. Insertion may worsen infection or spread it. Genital tract malignancy and marked uterine distortion are also contraindications.

Family Planning.question: 20) Unexplained genital bleeding should be considered before using:
Family Planning.exp: Unexplained genital bleeding is a contraindication to IUCD use. The cause should be evaluated before insertion. IUCD should not be used blindly in such cases.

Family Planning.question: 21) Copper IUCD can be used as emergency contraception when inserted:
Family Planning.exp: Copper IUD may be used as emergency contraception. The file mentions use within 5 days. It is the most effective emergency contraceptive method.

Family Planning.question: 22) The most effective emergency contraceptive method listed is:
Family Planning.exp: Copper IUD has effectiveness more than 99%. It can be inserted within 5 days. It is more effective than emergency pills.

Family Planning.question: 23) Levonorgestrel emergency pill is used within:
Family Planning.exp: Levonorgestrel emergency pill is used within 72 hours. It should be taken as early as possible. Effectiveness mentioned in the file is 85–90%.

Family Planning.question: 24) Ulipristal acetate emergency contraception is used within:
Family Planning.exp: Ulipristal acetate can be used within 120 hours or 5 days. Its effectiveness is more than 95%. It should still be taken as early as possible.

Family Planning.question: 25) Emergency pills mainly act by:
Family Planning.exp: Emergency pills delay ovulation. They also prevent fertilization. Copper IUD inhibits fertilization and prevents implantation.

Family Planning.question: 26) A common indication for emergency contraception is:
Family Planning.exp: Emergency contraception is used after unprotected intercourse. It is also used after contraceptive failure. Sexual assault is another indication.

Family Planning.question: 27) Condom slip or breakage is an indication for:
Family Planning.exp: Condom slip or breakage is contraceptive failure. Emergency contraception should be considered. Timing of the method is very important.

Family Planning.question: 28) Irregular menstrual bleeding after emergency contraception is:
Family Planning.option4: Side effect or point to remember
Family Planning.exp: Irregular menstrual bleeding may occur after emergency contraception. nCounseling reduces anxiety.

Family Planning.question: 29) Combined oral contraceptive pill mainly acts by:
Family Planning.exp: Combined oral contraceptive pills suppress ovulation. They also alter cervical mucus and endometrium. They are standard hormonal spacing methods.

Family Planning.question: 30) Progestogen-only pill is commonly selected for:
Family Planning.exp: Progestogen-only pill is commonly selected for breastfeeding or lactating mother. It is useful when estrogen is unsuitable. Contraindications should still be assessed.

Family Planning.question: 31) Mini-pill means:
Family Planning.exp: Mini-pill is the progestogen-only pill. It contains low-dose progestogen. It is often preferred during lactation.

Family Planning.question: 32) Centchroman is also known as:
Family Planning.exp: Centchroman is ormeloxifene. It is a non-steroidal oral contraceptive. It acts as a selective estrogen receptor modulator.

Family Planning.question: 33) DMPA is usually given every:
Family Planning.exp: DMPA is a long-acting injectable contraceptive. The file mentions it is commonly given every 3 months. It is a progestogen-only injectable method.

Family Planning.question: 34) NET-EN is usually given every:
Family Planning.exp: NET-EN is an injectable contraceptive. The file mentions it is given every 2 months. This is shorter than DMPA interval.

Family Planning.question: 35) Norplant and Jadelle are examples of:
Family Planning.exp: Norplant and Jadelle are subdermal implants. They are long-acting reversible progestogen-only methods. Implanon/Nexplanon are also examples.

Family Planning.question: 36) Vaginal ring and transdermal patch are:
Family Planning.exp: Vaginal ring and transdermal patch release hormones through non-oral routes. They are hormonal methods. They are alternatives to oral preparations.

Family Planning.question: 37) Menstrual regulation is classified as:
Family Planning.exp: Menstrual regulation is included under post-conceptional methods. It involves evacuation of uterine contents soon after missed period. It acts after conception or missed period.

Family Planning.question: 38) Menstrual induction means:
Family Planning.option4: Induction of menstrual bleeding after delayed period
Family Planning.exp: Menstrual induction means inducing menstrual bleeding after delayed period. It is grouped under post-conceptional methods. It is different from regular spacing contraception.

Family Planning.question: 39) Medical termination of pregnancy means:
Family Planning.option1: Termination under legally permitted and medically safe conditions
Family Planning.exp: Medical termination of pregnancy is termination under legal and safe medical conditions. It belongs to post-conceptional methods. It is not the same as routine contraception.

Family Planning.question: 40) Coitus interruptus means:
Family Planning.exp: Coitus interruptus is withdrawal method. The penis is withdrawn before ejaculation. It is unreliable due to pre-ejaculate and timing failure.

Family Planning.question: 41) Safe period method depends mainly on:
Family Planning.exp: Safe period method avoids intercourse during fertile period. It depends on accurate menstrual cycle calculation. Irregular cycles reduce reliability.

Family Planning.question: 42) Basal body temperature method identifies:
Family Planning.exp: Basal body temperature rises after ovulation. This method identifies the post-ovulatory rise. It requires careful daily recording.

Family Planning.question: 43) Billings method is based on:
Family Planning.exp: Billings method uses cyclical change in cervical mucus. It helps identify fertile days. It is a natural family planning method.

Family Planning.question: 44) Symptothermal method combines cervical mucus with:
Family Planning.exp: Symptothermal method combines multiple fertility signs. It includes temperature, cervical mucus and other ovulation symptoms. Combination improves identification of fertile period.

Family Planning.question: 45) Lactational amenorrhoea method is effective when the mother is amenorrhoeic, fully breastfeeding and within:
Family Planning.exp: Lactational amenorrhoea is effective only under strict criteria. Mother should be amenorrhoeic and fully or nearly fully breastfeeding. It applies within 6 months postpartum.

Family Planning.question: 46) Male sterilization is done by:
Family Planning.exp: Male sterilization is vasectomy. The vas deferens is occluded. No-scalpel vasectomy is also used.

Family Planning.question: 47) Female sterilization is done by:
Family Planning.exp: Female sterilization is tubectomy or tubal ligation. It may be done by mini-laparotomy or laparoscopy. It can be interval, postpartum or during caesarean section.

Family Planning.question: 48) After vasectomy, sterility is:
Family Planning.exp: Vasectomy does not give immediate sterility. Backup contraception is needed until clearance is confirmed. This point is important during counseling.

Family Planning.question: 49) Backup contraception after vasectomy is required because:
Family Planning.option1: Sperms may remain distal to the occlusion
Family Planning.exp: After vasectomy, sperm may remain in distal reproductive tract. So pregnancy can occur until semen is cleared. Backup contraception is required until semen analysis or programme clearance confirms azoospermia.

Family Planning.question: 50) No-scalpel vasectomy is a type of:
Family Planning.exp: No-scalpel vasectomy is a male sterilization technique. It occludes the vas deferens. It is intended for permanent contraception.

Family Planning.question: 51) Newly married couple is commonly advised:
Family Planning.exp: For a newly married couple, condom or OCP is appropriate. These are reversible spacing methods. They allow future fertility.

Family Planning.question: 52) Lactating mother is commonly advised:
Family Planning.exp: POP is commonly selected for lactating mother. It avoids estrogen-related concern. It is a reversible hormonal method.

Family Planning.question: 53) A mother with at least 2 living children may be advised:
Family Planning.exp: Terminal method is suitable when family size is completed. The file specifically mentions mother with at least 2 living children. Decision must be voluntary and informed.

Family Planning.question: 54) A mother who has just given birth may be advised:
Family Planning.exp: The file lists IUCD as an appropriate option after childbirth. Postpartum IUCD provides long-acting reversible contraception. Contraindications should still be excluded.

Family Planning.question: 55) The ideal contraceptive should be:
Family Planning.option2: Safe, effective, acceptable and reversible when desired
Family Planning.exp: An ideal contraceptive should be safe, effective and acceptable. It should be easy to use and affordable. For spacing, reversibility is important so fertility can return after stopping. Choice must match the couple’s need, age, parity and health status.

Family Planning.question: 56) The cafeteria approach in family planning means:
Family Planning.option3: Giving only one method to all couples
Family Planning.option4: Offering a variety of methods for informed choice
Family Planning.exp: Cafeteria approach means clients are offered a range of contraceptive options. The couple chooses after counseling about benefits, risks and suitability. It improves acceptance because the method matches personal preference. It also supports voluntary informed decision-making.

Family Planning.question: 57) Couple protection rate mainly indicates:
Family Planning.option1: Percentage of newborns vaccinated at birth
Family Planning.option3: Percentage of eligible couples effectively protected by contraception
Family Planning.option4: Percentage of pregnant women receiving ANC
Family Planning.exp: Couple protection rate measures contraceptive protection among eligible couples. It reflects how many couples are effectively protected from unwanted pregnancy. It is used as a family planning programme indicator. Higher CPR generally suggests better contraceptive coverage.

Family Planning.question: 58) Pearl index is used to measure:
Family Planning.exp: Pearl index measures contraceptive failure. It is usually expressed as pregnancies per 100 woman-years of exposure. Lower Pearl index means better contraceptive effectiveness. It allows comparison between different contraceptive methods.

Family Planning.question: 59) Method failure means pregnancy occurs due to:
Family Planning.option4: Failure of method despite correct use
Family Planning.exp: Method failure occurs even when the method is used correctly and consistently. It reflects inherent limitation of the contraceptive method. User failure is different and occurs due to wrong or inconsistent use. This distinction helps in counseling and programme evaluation.

Family Planning.question: 60) User failure in contraception is best described as pregnancy due to:
Family Planning.exp: User failure occurs when the contraceptive is not used properly. Examples include missed pills, condom breakage due to wrong use or irregular use. It is usually preventable by counseling and follow-up. It differs from method failure, where correct use still fails.

Family Planning.question: 61) The most suitable method for protection against both pregnancy and STI is:
Family Planning.exp: Male condom provides dual protection. It prevents pregnancy by acting as a barrier. It also reduces transmission of STI including HIV. Other methods like IUCD or pills do not protect against STI.

Family Planning.question: 62) A woman with active pelvic infection should preferably avoid:
Family Planning.exp: Active pelvic infection is a contraindication to IUCD use. IUCD insertion may aggravate or spread infection. A non-invasive temporary method can be selected until infection is treated. Proper screening before IUCD insertion is essential.

Family Planning.question: 63) The method most dependent on correct daily intake is:
Family Planning.exp: Oral contraceptive pills require regular intake. Missed pills can reduce contraceptive effectiveness. This is why counseling on correct use is important. Long-acting methods like IUCD or implants are less user-dependent.

Family Planning.question: 64) The contraceptive method with no immediate effect after procedure is:
Family Planning.exp: Vasectomy does not cause immediate sterility. Sperms already present beyond the occlusion may remain for some time. Backup contraception is needed until clearance is confirmed. This should always be explained before and after the procedure.

Family Planning.question: 65) Which method is long-acting reversible contraception?
Family Planning.exp: IUCD is a long-acting reversible contraceptive. It provides protection for a long duration. Fertility usually returns after removal.

Family Planning.question: 66) Which method is most clearly unreliable due to timing failure and pre-ejaculate?
Family Planning.exp: Withdrawal or coitus interruptus is unreliable. Pre-ejaculate may contain sperm or timing may fail. It requires high self-control and gives no STI protection.

Family Planning.question: 67) Which contraceptive is most suitable when estrogen is unsuitable?
Family Planning.exp: POP is useful when estrogen is unsuitable. It contains only progestogen. It is also commonly selected during breastfeeding.

Family Planning.question: 68) The contraceptive action of LAM is mainly due to:
Family Planning.exp: Lactational amenorrhoea works by suppressing ovulation during exclusive or near-exclusive breastfeeding. Frequent suckling suppresses hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian activity. It is reliable only if mother is amenorrhoeic, fully breastfeeding and within 6 months postpartum. If any criterion is absent, another contraceptive should be advised.

Family Planning.question: 69) A couple with completed family and desire for permanent contraception should be counseled for:
Family Planning.exp: Terminal methods are intended for permanent limitation of family size. They include vasectomy and tubectomy. They should be chosen only after informed voluntary decision.

Family Planning.question: 70) A method used after unprotected intercourse but before expected pregnancy confirmation is:
Family Planning.exp: Emergency contraception is used after unprotected intercourse or contraceptive failure. Examples include LNG pill, UPA and copper IUD. It should be used as early as possible.
